description.narrative:
CAFOD is the lead agency in Ethiopia for the NGOs and Humanitarian Reform Project Phase 2 (NHRP2), and hosts a project manager (currently a consultant) to work with the NGO humanitarian community in country and liaise on policy and advocacy internationally.
The project aims to identify and address challenges in the implementation of the humanitarian reform agenda at the country level in 5 project implementation countries as well as at the international policy level.
Enhancing and influencing the UN-led humanitarian reform agenda has been a policy priority theme for CAFOD’s humanitarian policy and advocacy since 2008. The agency participated in the first phase of the NHRP, but did not have an opportunity to play a more central role until this project, which represents an exciting opportunity for CAFOD to raise its influence and profile by leading the project in Ethiopia.
Ethiopia was one of four countries benefiting from the NHRPI, during which a Humanitarian NGO Forum (HINGO) was established. 44 international humanitarian agencies are members of the HINGO with the active participation of some 20 INGOs. The HINGO was established to develop a structured and collaborative NGO engagement with humanitarian partners, including with the Ethiopia Humanitarian Country Team, the HRF and Government of Ethiopia. CAFOD has been a prominent member of the HINGO and is among the lead agencies in the country on implementing global initiatives such as LEGS, Sphere and the Good Enough Guide. Unfortunately national NGOs have no representation through HINGO as its ToRs state membership is exclusively for international NGOs.
